Lesson 3 of 5

Load balancing

Load balancers distribute requests across healthy backends and are the main control point for availability, failover, and safe scaling at the service edge.

25-35 min HLD flow Networking, edge, and request routing 4 guided stops

Why this lesson matters

They are foundational because almost every stateless tier depends on balancing to survive failures and scale horizontally.

Start with this framing

Interview framing

They are foundational because almost every stateless tier depends on balancing to survive failures and scale horizontally.

What to say first

  • Explain how requests are distributed and how unhealthy nodes are removed.

    Show likely answer

  • Choose L4 or L7 based on needed routing logic.

    Show likely answer
    • Choose L4 or L7 based on needed routing logic.
    • Choose L4 for simple, high-throughput transport routing
    • L7 routing is worth the cost when you need host, path, header, cookie, or auth-aware decisions, plus features such as TLS termination, canaries, or application-level health checks.

  • Mention connection draining and rolling deploy behavior.

    Show likely answer
    • Mention connection draining and rolling deploy behavior.
    • Keep deploys safe by draining connections, removing a node from rotation before shutdown, using health checks to gate traffic, and rolling out gradually while watching backend error rates.
    • Balancers use health checks and connection draining to stop sending users to degraded instances during deploys or incidents.

Study section

L4 vs. L7 balancing

Layer 4 balancing routes by transport metadata, while Layer 7 balancing understands HTTP details and can route by host, path, or headers.

Call these points out explicitly

  • Choose L4 for simple, high-throughput transport routing

    Show likely answer
    • Choose L4 for simple, high-throughput transport routing
    • Choose L4 for simple, high-throughput transport routing
    • A strong load-balancer answer also names the trade-off: L4 is cheaper and faster for simple transport routing, while L7 buys more control at higher operational cost.

  • Choose L7 when you need sticky sessions, canarying, or auth-aware policies

    Show likely answer
    • Choose L7 when you need sticky sessions, canarying, or auth-aware policies
    • Choose L7 when you need sticky sessions, canarying, or auth-aware policies
    • L7 routing is worth the cost when you need host, path, header, cookie, or auth-aware decisions, plus features such as TLS termination, canaries, or application-level health checks.

  • Managed platforms often combine both layers

    Show likely answer
    • Managed platforms often combine both layers
    • Managed platforms often combine both layers
    • Modern balancers often terminate TLS, emit metrics, apply rate limits, and support weighted rollouts.

Operational features

Modern balancers often terminate TLS, emit metrics, apply rate limits, and support weighted rollouts.

Call these points out explicitly

  • Session affinity can help stateful migrations but hurts elasticity

    • Session affinity can help stateful migrations but hurts elasticity

Common pitfalls

What to avoid

  • Using sticky sessions as a default instead of fixing state management.
  • Ignoring TLS termination and certificate rotation.
  • Forgetting that load balancers are also failure domains.

Interview prompts

Practice aloud

  • When does L7 routing justify the extra complexity?

    Show likely answer
    • L7 routing is worth the cost when you need host, path, header, cookie, or auth-aware decisions, plus features such as TLS termination, canaries, or application-level health checks.
    • A strong load-balancer answer also names the trade-off: L4 is cheaper and faster for simple transport routing, while L7 buys more control at higher operational cost.
    • Choose L4 or L7 based on needed routing logic.

  • How would you keep deploys safe behind a load balancer?

    Show likely answer
    • Keep deploys safe by draining connections, removing a node from rotation before shutdown, using health checks to gate traffic, and rolling out gradually while watching backend error rates.
    • A strong load-balancer answer also names the trade-off: L4 is cheaper and faster for simple transport routing, while L7 buys more control at higher operational cost.
    • Balancers use health checks and connection draining to stop sending users to degraded instances during deploys or incidents.

  • Why is session affinity usually a temporary compromise?

    Show likely answer
    • Session affinity is usually temporary because it hides stateful coupling, weakens elasticity and failover, and should eventually be replaced by stateless sessions or shared state.
    • Session affinity can help stateful migrations but hurts elasticity
